title: Long XOM — Iran/Hormuz Escalation + Permian + Freeport LNG Structural Divergence
entry: Long XOM $138–145 at Monday July 13 open. XOM is the highest-quality way to hold the Iran/Hormuz oil spike: unlike the broader XLE ETF (already in the book), XOM specifically benefits through Permian Basin production (~4.3M BOE/day, entirely onshore US — zero Hormuz exposure) and its 18B cubic feet/day Freeport LNG export capacity (Asian buyers sourcing alternatives to Persian Gulf piped gas bid up spot LNG, directly improving XOM's export margins). Enter 60% at open, hold 40% for any intraday pullback toward $138 on a market-wide risk-off flush if the SPX opens sharply lower. Do not initiate above $147 — at that level the intraday oil-spike premium has fully repriced XOM and the risk/reward compresses.
stop_loss: $128 daily close — at that level WTI has likely returned sustainably below $65 (ceasefire confirmed + Hormuz fully reopened + OPEC+ releasing strategic reserves), which removes the Hormuz supply-disruption premium entirely and returns XOM to fair value under the prior $65-70 WTI equilibrium. A $128 close also implies the upstream oil-price thesis has been invalidated without the countervailing LNG-spot thesis materializing.
targets: $152 — WTI sustains above $77 for 3 consecutive sessions; XOM trades up 7.7% from entry on elevated near-term oil prices; Q3 2026 production guidance implied above $78 WTI; cover 40% of position at this quick profit-take level within the first 1–2 weeks

$161 — WTI breaks $80 (September rate-hike trip wire per the July 13 morning briefing) before August CPI (released August 12); XOM guides Q3 revenue above $90B at an Aug 1 investor day or earns a sell-side upgrade consensus to $163+ price target; cover 40% at this base-case level as rate-hike fears bite broader market but energy rotation accelerates

$171 — blue sky: Iran conflict extends beyond August with no ceasefire in sight; WTI sustains $85+; XOM's Q3 EPS beats by >15% on oil price variance vs Q3 guidance; Freeport LNG spot contract repricing adds incremental $2B to annual revenue vs prior year; hold final 20% toward August earnings
risk_reward: 1:2.3 to third target (entry $141, stop $128 = risk $13; T3 $171 = reward $30)
catalyst: US and Iranian forces have exchanged strikes over the weekend of July 12-13, with Iran claiming the Strait of Hormuz formally closed to commercial shipping. WTI is up 2.5–4.2% to ~$73–74 at the July 13 open (from approximately $70-71 on Friday July 11). XOM's Q2 2026 earnings are scheduled for August 1; the Iran escalation will add approximately $3-5/barrel to XOM's embedded oil price assumption for Q3 guidance, creating a positive earnings revision catalyst. Additionally, the Freeport LNG export terminal (XOM ownership stake) benefits from any Asian LNG spot price spike driven by buyers seeking alternatives to Persian Gulf-sourced gas.
thesis:
XOM is differentiated from the XLE ETF (already active in the book at $54.95 entry) in three critical ways relevant to the Iran/Hormuz thesis. First, XOM's Permian production is entirely landlocked US supply — the Permian Basin is in West Texas, connected by pipeline to Gulf of Mexico refineries and export terminals. Iran closing the Strait of Hormuz has zero direct supply-chain impact on XOM's Permian output, but WTI pricing increases on Hormuz disruption flow dollar-for-dollar into Permian margins. This is the cleanest possible oil-price exposure: benefit from the disruption premium without operational exposure to the disruption geography.

Second, Freeport LNG (XOM is a significant stakeholder in Freeport LNG's export capacity) becomes structurally more valuable as a Hormuz alternative. Approximately 20% of global LNG supply transits through or near the Strait of Hormuz from Qatar, Abu Dhabi, and Oman. If those shipments are disrupted, Asian buyers (Japan, South Korea, China) immediately redirect to spot LNG from US Gulf Coast exporters — of which Freeport LNG is a major source. Freeport's 18B cubic feet/day export capacity operating at full spot pricing adds materially to XOM's LNG-segment revenue. This is a non-linear upside to XOM's base case that XLE (which is weighted toward producers, not LNG exporters) does not capture.

Third, XOM's Q2 2026 earnings on August 1 will embed whatever WTI level prevails through mid-July in its Q3 guidance range. If WTI holds $73+ through the week of July 14-17 (through CPI and Warsh testimony), XOM's Q3 guidance midpoint moves meaningfully higher than what was implied at the Q1 earnings in May. The buy side will model this ahead of the August 1 print, creating a pre-earnings drift. At the current $141 price, XOM trades at approximately 11.5x 2026 consensus EPS of $12.20 — a multiple that expands as oil-price revisions raise the EPS denominator toward $13-14.

The counter-party is the XOM bear who argues: (1) WTI at $73 is not a lasting equilibrium — OPEC+ has spare capacity above 3M BOE/day and will increase production to offset any Hormuz disruption premium once the political situation stabilizes; (2) XOM's Pioneer acquisition cost basis is fully embedded at the current $141 price, so incremental oil upside is mostly already priced; (3) a September rate hike (September probability now 60%) increases XOM's cost of capital for its ongoing deepwater development pipeline (Guyana, Brazil), compressing the terminal value. The bull response: OPEC+ spare capacity is priced in to current WTI; what the market is NOT pricing is a sustained Hormuz closure lasting 2-4 weeks — which would create a supply shock OPEC+ cannot cover from existing production levels on a daily flow basis.
bull_case: Iran and CENTCOM cannot resolve the Hormuz dispute diplomatically within 7 days; tankers divert around the Cape of Good Hope (adding 15-21 days to voyage). WTI spikes to $82 by July 21 (the day before the Warsh follow-up hearing). XOM rallies to $158 on pre-earnings oil-price modeling. Freeport LNG spot contract repricing confirmed in July port data. XOM's August 1 Q2 earnings beat on oil-price variance and Freeport LNG upside — guidance raised to $13+ EPS 2026. Stock targets $171+ on the combination of beat and bullish Q3 guidance.
bear_case: Iran-US ceasefire confirmed within 72 hours with CENTCOM announcing Hormuz open above 90% normal capacity. WTI falls from $74 back toward $67-68 as Hormuz supply premium deflates. XOM gives back the July 13 oil-spike premium and returns toward $134-136. Position reaches stop ($128) only if WTI falls below $65 on OPEC+ oversupply; at $128 stop the loss is ~9% from entry on a 4% position = ~36bps total portfolio drag. The defined stop limits downside.
invalidation: WTI daily close below $68 (ceasefire confirmed + Hormuz reopened + OPEC+ releasing emergency reserves); OR Iran-US ceasefire announcement with verified Hormuz commercial traffic above 70% of normal by July 17 (directly removes the supply-disruption premium); OR XOM Q2 pre-announcement signals a miss on Permian volumes due to pipeline constraints (company-specific negative); OR September rate-hike probability rises above 85% and energy stocks begin pricing demand-destruction from the macro tightening channel rather than supply disruption
